label: First copy step (input = first original token, right after <DEL>) in long sequences, token-gated
explanation: Fires almost only at step t = L+1, the first copy-phase step after the delimiter, where the input is the fed-back first original token and the model is outputting original token 1 (recall_idx==1 covers 99.6% of activations and 99.9% of mass). It never fires in the original phase, and fires essentially never at the delimiter or at later copy steps. Within that step it is gated by sequence length and by the identity of the first token. Rate rises steeply with L: about 72% of mass is at L=9 and 24% at L=8, with almost nothing for L<=6. Some first tokens drive it much harder: 0, x, c and f carry the largest activations and the top examples. Others such as t, w, 3, v, p, r, l and j almost never activate it even at L=9. The predicate (L>=8 and first token in a favoured set of 14) gets dev F1 0.70 and mass recall 0.87. The token preference is graded, not a clean set, so precision is incomplete.
